note: Adapted from Emerson’s 1952 original English description (the paper first describes this species); measurements translated verbatim from Table 14 of the original, in millimetres. The original did not describe the worker.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other known alates of the genus by the vertical position of the ocellus and by only a very small white area of the ocellus being visible from above. The soldier differs from C. cumulans in the more angular lateral margins of the labrum and the proportionally narrower middle of the postmentum; C. silvestrii has less angular lateral margins of the labrum, straighter and more parallel sides of the head, and more parallel sides of the postmentum; C. bolivianus has evenly rounded lateral margins of the labrum without lateral angles, and the right mandible from the notch angle to the tip is 0.67—0.76 mm long.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale reddish brown, frontal gland plate pale yellow; labrum pale yellow; postclypeus pale yellow; pronotum paler than the head, about the same colour as the labrum; tibiae concolorous with the femora; wing membrane transparent, anterior margin and radius brown or yellow. Head sparsely or densely covered with medium-length setae; pronotum with setae and some short hairs; tergites with marginal setae and some short hairs on the disc. Head broadly oval. Frontal gland plate oval or round, rather large, not longer than the ocellus, its surface convex but not raised above the surrounding head surface. Eyes rather large, separated from the lower margin of the head by about 1/6—1/7 of their diameter. Ocelli broadly oval, separated from the eyes by less than their own width, the upper margin raised above the head surface and the lower margin sunk, so that the ocellar surface is nearly vertical and only a very small white area is visible from above. Antennae 15- or 16-segmented. Postclypeus about half as long as wide. Anterior margin of the pronotum broadly concave, anterior angles rounded, sides curved and narrowed posteriorly, middle of the posterior margin distinctly notched, with a distinct oval depression near the anterolateral angles.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dull yellow, labrum tinged with pale brown; pronotum yellow; legs pale yellow; abdomen pale yellow. Head with many setae and some shorter hairs, but not forming a contrasting short hair blanket; postmentum with short hairs and about 2 anterior setae; posterior hemisphere of the pronotum with many setae and some short hairs; tergites with a median row of setae and another row near the posterior margin; sternites with setae and sparse short hairs. Head nearly rectangular, sides slightly curved and slightly narrowed anteriorly, posterior angles and posterior margin rounded. Frontal tube rather large, covering the base of the postclypeus. Narrowest part of the postmentum about 7/9—7/10 of the greatest width (0.35—0.38:0.50 mm). Antennae 15-segmented. Lateral angles of the labrum distinct but slightly rounded, all greater than a right angle, the margin between the lateral angles and the base of the white median lobe slightly concave or nearly straight. Anterior margin of the pronotum distinctly or indistinctly concave. Measurements (mm; original Table 14, n=18—25): head length including mandibles 2.74—3.47 (mean 2.98); head length to the tip of the frontal tube 1.88—2.29 (2.00); head length to the lateral mandibular bases 1.91—2.59 (2.18); head width 1.50—1.85 (1.64); head thickness 1.15—1.47 (1.26); frontal tube length 0.34—0.41 (0.37); labrum width 0.51—0.63 (0.56); left mandible length 1.04—1.17 (1.10); right mandible length from the notch 0.56—0.65 (0.60); pronotum length 0.47—0.59 (0.52); pronotum width 0.81—1.00 (0.87); hind tibia length 1.37—1.65 (1.47).
